purpose: Reference species used to validate the pH 7.4 protonation rule set. Each case records the EXPECTED atom-mapped species AND the pKa evidence behind it. Evidence tiers are honest: a PubChem link proves STRUCTURE, not solution ionisation, and is therefore recorded separately in 'pubchem_structure_url' and NEVER counted as a pKa source.

evidence_tiers.COMPOUND_SPECIFIC_EXPERIMENTAL: Measured pKa for this exact compound, on a source that was actually fetched and quoted.
evidence_tiers.CURATED_EXPERIMENTAL_COMPILATION: Experimental value from a curated compilation (e.g. the ACS-hosted Jencks/Westheimer table); primary paper not independently fetched.
evidence_tiers.SECONDARY_REVIEW: Number appears on a fetched peer-reviewed page, but the chain of custody stops at a review or textbook rather than a measurement.
evidence_tiers.NO_SOURCE_FOUND: No experimental pKa was verifiable from any fetchable source. Reported as such rather than substituting a predicted value.

verification_note: Every pKa, URL and quote was verified by loading the page. No DOI, author, year or journal was reconstructed from memory. Two compounds (fosfomycin, pentamidine) have NO verifiable experimental pKa: the values that circulate for both are software PREDICTIONS (Chemicalize; DrugBank) that have been laundered into prose as though measured. They are recorded as NO_SOURCE_FOUND rather than cited.

cases.name: benzoic_acid
cases.conditions: 25 C, aqueous; extrapolated to zero ionic strength (I varied 0.0013-0.50 M NaCl)
cases.pka_source_citation: Khouri SJ. Titrimetric Study of the Solubility and Dissociation of Benzoic Acid in Water. Am J Anal Chem. 2015;6(5).
cases.verified_quote: The value of estimated logKa from the plot is -4.176 +/- 0.01035, which its inverse (4.176) represents pKa of benzoic acid at 25 C.

cases.name: acetic_acid
cases.conditions: aqueous; T/I not stated in the compilation
cases.pka_source_citation: pKa Data Compiled by R. Williams (Jencks/Westheimer), ACS Organic Division, upd. 2022-04-07; value ref. 20 = Dippy JFJ et al., J Chem Soc. 1959, 2492.
cases.caveat: Curated experimental compilation, not the primary paper. Harned & Ehlers (4.756, 25 C) was not fetchable.

cases.name: methanesulfonic_acid
cases.pka_value: -0.6 (compilation); literature CONFLICT, ca. -1.9 also widely cited
cases.conditions: not stated; strong-acid pKa is method-dependent (H0 acidity function vs thermodynamic cycle)
cases.pka_source_citation: pKa Data Compiled by R. Williams, ACS Organic Division; value ref. 31 = Brownstein S, Stillman AE, J Phys Chem. 1959;63:2061.
cases.caveat: GENUINE LITERATURE CONFLICT: the commonly quoted ca. -1.9 (Guthrie, Can J Chem 1978) could not be verified on a fetchable page. Values disagree by >1 log unit. Irrelevant to speciation at pH 7.4 (fully deprotonated either way).

cases.name: fosfomycin
cases.caveat: NO experimental fosfomycin pKa was verifiable. The only value printed in a peer-reviewed paper we could open is EXPLICITLY a Chemicalize PREDICTION (1.25 / 7.82; Bianchi et al., ACS Infect Dis 2024, PMC10789261). The 1.8/6.5 pair circulating in search results traces to a paywalled J Mol Struct paper that could not be opened. A predicted value must not be reported as measured.

cases.name: taurine
cases.ionisable_site: sulfonic acid; primary ammonium (zwitterion at physiological pH)
cases.pka_source_citation: pKa Data Compiled by R. Williams, ACS Organic Division, amino-acid table; value ref. 6 = Dawson RMC et al., Data for Biochemical Research, Clarendon Press, 1959.
cases.caveat: pKa1 poorly constrained across sources (1.05-1.51); irrelevant above pH 2 - the sulfonate is anionic at any biological pH.

cases.name: tetrazole
cases.pka_source_citation: Maji et al. Exploring tetrazole chemistry. Front Chem. 2025.
cases.verified_quote: Tetrazole behaves as a weak acid with a pKa of approximately 4.89, comparable to propanoic acid.
cases.caveat: WEAK CHAIN OF CUSTODY: the fetched page is a peer-reviewed REVIEW attributing the number to ANOTHER REVIEW, not to a measurement. The candidate primary (J Chem Eng Data, 10.1021/je010031p) is paywalled. Deliberately NOT tiered as COMPOUND_SPECIFIC_EXPERIMENTAL.

cases.name: warfarin
cases.pka_value: 4.85-5.15 (literature range); 4.46 +/- 0.05 measured on sodium warfarin in the fetched study
cases.conditions: see source; range from spectrophotometric and capillary-electrophoresis determinations
cases.pka_source_citation: Kaufelde et al. Taste-Masked Microparticles of Sodium Warfarin. Pharmaceutics. 2026.
cases.verified_quote: Warfarin is ... with the experimentally estimated pKa in the range from 4.85 to 5.15
cases.caveat: The canonical '5.05' (Hiskey 1962) could NOT be verified on any fetchable page and is therefore NOT cited here.

cases.name: doxycycline
cases.ionisable_site: tricarbonyl/enol; phenolic beta-diketone; C4 dimethylammonium (assignment is literature convention, NOT stated by the fetched source)
cases.conditions: aqueous; original determination by potentiometric titration
cases.pka_source_citation: Racovita S et al. Int J Mol Sci. 2024;25(14):7871. doi:10.3390/ijms25147871
cases.verified_quote: DCH can act as an anion, cation or zwitterion and therefore possesses several values of the acid dissociation constant (pKa1 = 3.02, pKa2 = 7.97, pKa3 = 9.15).
cases.caveat: SITE ASSIGNMENT IS INFERENCE, not sourced. Note pKa2 = 7.97 sits close to 7.4.

cases.name: benzamidine
cases.pka_source_citation: Iddon B, Hunter CA. Solvation-Enhanced Salt Bridges. J Am Chem Soc. 2024;146(41):28580-28588. Attributed therein to Albert A, Goldacre R, Phillips J. J Chem Soc. 1948:2240-2249.

cases.name: guanidine
cases.pka_source_citation: Caine BA, Dardonville C, Popelier PLA. ACS Omega. 2018;3(4):3835-3850.
cases.verified_quote: For guanidine itself, we use a value of 13.6 as per the Foye's Principles of Medicinal Chemistry.
cases.caveat: Provenance chain stops at a TEXTBOOK, not a primary measurement. Tiered down accordingly.

cases.name: metformin
cases.ionisable_site: biguanide; ONE charge at pH 7.4 -> net +1
cases.pka_source_citation: Castaneda-Sanchez et al. Int J Mol Sci. 2025;26(13):5925.
cases.caveat: The FDA-label figure of 12.4 was NOT cited: every accessdata.fda.gov URL returned 404, so it could not be verified.

cases.name: pentamidine
cases.caveat: NO experimental pentamidine pKa exists in any fetchable source. The widely circulated 'pKa 12.1' - stated as fact and WITHOUT a reference in a PLoS Pathogens paper (PMC4734766) - is almost certainly DrugBank's PREDICTED 12.13 laundered into prose; a 2022 paper (PMC8880300) explicitly labels it 'predicted'. The +2 state used here is justified as a CLOSE-ANALOG inference from benzamidine (experimental 11.6), and is labelled as such - never as a pentamidine measurement.

cases.name: propranolol
cases.pka_source_citation: Zhou X et al. Sci Rep. 2018;8:3912, Table 1 (Experimental pKa); dataset from Luan F et al. Pharm Res. 2005;22:1454-1460.

cases.name: azithromycin
cases.ionisable_site: two basic tertiary amines (desosamine dimethylamino; macrolactone ring N). NO fetched source assigns which pKa belongs to which N.
cases.pka_source_citation: Zheng S, Matzneller P, Zeitlinger M, Schmidt S. Antimicrob Agents Chemother. 2014;58(11):6675-6684.
cases.verified_quote: AZM is a diprotic base (pKa1, 8.1; pKa2, 8.8)
cases.caveat: The popular 8.74/9.45 pair could NOT be verified and is NOT used. Site assignment is NOT claimed. Either way the compound is +2 at pH 7.4 - which is what this repo's rule must preserve.

cases.name: acetaminophen
cases.pka_source_citation: Walton-Raaby M et al. Antioxidants (Basel). 2023;12(7):1420, Table 2.

cases.name: imidazole
cases.pka_source_citation: Tilly DP, Heeb J-P, Webb SJ, Clayden J. Nat Commun. 2023;14:2647.
cases.caveat: pKa 6.95 sits BELOW 7.4 but within ~0.5 units - only ~26% protonated at 7.4. The repo leaves imidazole NEUTRAL; this is a rounding decision the reader can now check.

cases.name: cysteamine
cases.pka_source_citation: Csorba et al. Int J Mol Sci. 2024;25(3):1623. Attributed therein to Mirzahosseini A, Noszal B. J Pharm Biomed Anal. 2014;95:184-192.
cases.caveat: SECONDARY REPORTING: the primary (Mirzahosseini 2014) is paywalled and was not opened.

cases.name: aniline
cases.pka_source_citation: Gross KC, Seybold PG. Int J Quantum Chem. 2000. pKa values taken from the review of Albert & Serjeant.
cases.caveat: Free base >99.9% dominant at pH 7.4 - confirms the repo's decision to leave anilines neutral.

cases.name: benzenesulfonamide
cases.conditions: potentiometric titration, I = 0.052 M NaCl, +/-0.2 pH units
cases.pka_source_citation: Krishnamurthy VM et al. Chem Asian J. 2007. doi:10.1002/asia.200600360
cases.caveat: >99.8% un-ionised at pH 7.4 - confirms leaving sulfonamides neutral.

cases.name: phenylboronic_acid
cases.ionisable_site: BORON centre - NOT a simple O-H loss: trigonal PhB(OH)2 + 2 H2O <-> tetrahedral PhB(OH)3- + H3O+ (hydroxide addition to the Lewis-acidic boron)
cases.conditions: 25 +/- 1 C, aqueous, I = 0.1 M KCl; potentiometric and spectrophotometric titration
cases.pka_source_citation: Sporzynski A, Adamczyk-Wozniak A, Zarzeczanska D, et al. Molecules. 2024;29(11):2713. doi:10.3390/molecules29112713
cases.caveat: ~4% anionic boronate at pH 7.4; the neutral trigonal form dominates.

cases.name: caffeine
cases.ionisable_site: ring N (very weakly basic); no relevant acidic proton near neutral pH
cases.pka_source_citation: Recent Advances in Electrochemical Sensors for Caffeine Determination. Sensors (Basel). 2022. (PMC9735645)
cases.verified_quote: Sarakhman [83] discussed caffeine's nature as a weak base (pKa~0.7)
cases.caveat: The apparent primary (Spiro M et al., J Chem Soc Faraday Trans 1. 1989;85:4259) is 403-blocked and was NOT verified. Conclusion is robust regardless: caffeine is >99.99% neutral at pH 7.4.

cases.name: sildenafil
cases.ionisable_site: N-methylpiperazine basic N; pyrimidinone amide N-H (ampholyte)
cases.pka_source_citation: Sildenafil 4.0 - Integrated Synthetic Chemistry, Formulation and Analytical Strategies. Molecules. 2021. (PMC8071249)
cases.verified_quote: the moderately strong, basic functional NH-piperazine featuring a pKa1 value of 6.78 and the weak acidic HN- pyrimidone amide featuring pKa2 value of 9.12
cases.caveat: CONFIRMS THE FIX: basic pKa 6.78 => only ~19% protonated at pH 7.4, so the NEUTRAL free base (~81%) dominates. The old rule's +1 was wrong.

cases.name: lisinopril
cases.pka_value: logK1 10.75 (primary amine); logK2 7.13 (secondary amine); logK3 3.13 and logK4 1.63 (carboxylates)
cases.ionisable_site: primary/terminal amine; secondary amine; proline-ring carboxylate; side-chain carboxylate - WITH explicit site assignment in the source
cases.conditions: 25.0 C, ionic strength 0.15 M; potentiometry + Yasuda-Shedlovsky + 1H NMR-pH titration
cases.pka_source_citation: Takacs-Novak K, Deak K, Beni S, Volgyi G. Physico-chemical Profiling of the ACE-inhibitor Lisinopril: Acid-base Properties. ADMET & DMPK. 2013;1(2):6-16. doi:10.5599/admet.1.2.3
cases.verified_quote: log K1 = 10.75 +/- 0.01, log K2 = 7.13 +/- 0.01, log K3 = 3.13 +/- 0.01, log K4 = 1.63 +/- 0.01 ... At the pH of the plasma, the monoanion (HLis-) is the dominant form (more than 60%)
cases.caveat: DRIVES A RECLASSIFICATION. The source's own speciation table at pH 7.4 gives HLis- 65.04% and the NEUTRAL double-zwitterion H2Lis 34.93%. A 35% minor species is too large to discard, so lisinopril is reclassified AMBIGUOUS and docked in BOTH states.

cases.name: losartan
cases.ionisable_site: tetrazole N-H (acidic) and imidazole N. THE SOURCE DOES NOT ASSIGN WHICH CONSTANT BELONGS TO WHICH RING.
cases.conditions: thermodynamic constants extrapolated over I = 0.01-1.0, at 25 and 37 C; pH-spectrophotometric titration (SPECFIT32/SQUAD84)
cases.pka_source_citation: Meloun M, Syrovy T, Vrana A. Anal Chim Acta. 2005;533(1):97-110. doi:10.1016/j.aca.2004.11.007
cases.verified_quote: for losartan pKa,1T=3.63(1) and 3.57(3), pKa,2T=4.84(1) and 4.80(3)
cases.caveat: SITE ASSIGNMENT IS INFERENCE, not sourced. Conclusion holds regardless: BOTH constants are far below 7.4, so the tetrazole is DEPROTONATED and the imidazole NEUTRAL at pH 7.4 => net -1. This is the bug the old rule got wrong (it docked losartan neutral).
